passages.anchor: p. 1 title/organizer/as-at/visa; p. 6 Art. 2.3, German and English approval clauses
passages.text: VLN Sport GmbH & Co. KG organizes the series, supported by VLN VV GmbH & Co. KG. Part 1 is as at 12 June 2026 and carries DMSB approval/visa 970/26. The German approval clause prints 16 February 2025, while parallel English prints 16 February 2026. The discrepancy is unresolved; neither date establishes issue or commencement of this consolidated version.

passages.text: The currently valid listed FIA/DMSB instruments, DMSB circuit Appendices 1 and 2, NLS Parts 1-3, approved bulletins and event regulations apply. Only the DMSB-approved German text is binding. Interpretation involves the clerk/race director with stewards and organizer; final interpretation rests with DMSB sporting jurisdiction. This does not identify an exact DMSB edition or establish a universal precedence ladder.

passages.anchor: p. 9 Art. 4, matching Qualifiers and points-allocation paragraph
passages.text: The two ADAC 24h Nurburgring Qualifiers races run under their event regulations. Points for all events listed in the NLS series calendar are awarded under these series regulations. This scoring-scope wording is present in A1; it does not establish that a particular Qualifiers race was completed or earned points.

passages.anchor: p. 51 Art. 25, registration/fee and nonregistered participants
passages.text: Registered drivers and competitors/teams are eligible for championship classifications A-I only after receipt of registration and its fee. Earlier results do not count. Nonregistered participants receive no championship points and appear only in event classifications. Additional Cup/Trophy conditions apply.

passages.anchor: pp. 51-52 Art. 25.1, scope/final class rank/actual starters
passages.text: Classifications A-F, including the annual overall championship but excluding G/H/I, use actual class placing in official final race results and the Arts. 25.1.1-25.1.2 tables. Nonregistered participants are not deleted to promote registered participants, except for classification/sporting penalties. Class starters are vehicles actually starting by crossing the start line after the start signal or subsequently starting from the pit lane, not registered entrants, qualifiers or finishers.

passages.anchor: p. 53 Art. 25.1.1 4h matrix and Art. 25.1.2 6h matrix
passages.text: The allocation tables depend on actual class starters and final class rank. For class rank 1 and class-starter bands 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or more, the full-points 4-hour awards are respectively 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 11, 15; the full-points 6-hour awards are respectively 3, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 19. These are the complete winner rows, not the lower-rank rows. A one-starter class can score; seven starters is a field-size band, not a minimum eligibility threshold. No continuous formula or general points-rounding instruction is established by these allocation paragraphs.

passages.anchor: p. 52 Art. 25.1, shortened/stopped-race duration bands a/b
passages.text: If scheduled distance is shortened or a stopped race is not resumed, a 4-hour race lasting up to 80 minutes has no classification; over 80 through 160 minutes gives half points; over 160 minutes gives full points. For a 6-hour race, up to 120 minutes has no classification; over 120 through 250 minutes gives half points; over 250 minutes gives full points. The boundary is 250, not 240. These are duration bands within A-F allocation, not a 75% distance threshold; their application to G/H/I is not established here.

translation.method: assistant factual translation verified against PDF extraction
translation.source_anchor: p. 52 Art. 25.1, shortened/stopped-race duration bands a/b

passages.text: The winner completes the most laps; equal distances are ordered by shorter elapsed time including imposed time penalties. Classification requires at least 70% of the class winner's distance and 50% of the overall winner's distance, each commercially rounded, and crossing the finish/timing line within 20 minutes after the overall winner is flagged. Finish and counted laps must be under the vehicle's own engine power. The final lap must combine the GP course and Nordschleife. Vehicles entering the pit lane while being flagged can cross its extended timing line; those already in the pit lane when the leader is flagged are not classified. Results become final after technical checks and any protest/appeal proceedings. An exact equal-distance/equal-time dead heat is not resolved here.

passages.anchor: pp. 41-42 Art. 18.5, stoppage/restart, especially p. 42 DMSB reference
passages.text: Stoppage classification refers to DMSB circuit Arts. 16.4 and/or 16.5. The last counted lap must end over the timing line under the vehicle's own engine power. The extracted restart clauses distinguish a leader below two laps from above two laps. Exactly two laps and the incorporated DMSB details remain unresolved; this is not a complete restart algorithm.

passages.text: For A-F, ten or nine completed races use the best eight results. Drivers/competitors/teams completing eight or fewer count those results without a discard. A completed counting race is a classified race in which that vehicle crossed the start line. A disqualification cannot be discarded. These season-total rules do not establish the actual number of completed races or an individual race award.

translation.method: assistant factual translation verified against PDF extraction

passages.text: A driver starting two cars nominates the car for driver-championship points on the signed double-starter list by Saturday 08:00; without nomination the lower start number is used. Class classifications separately count the placing in each of two different classes, or the better placing when both cars are in one class. This double-start exception does not establish division or duplication of points among co-drivers.

translation.method: assistant factual translation verified against PDF extraction

passages.text: NLS Speed Trophy H is a separate award: registered competitors/teams identified by car start number score for top-20 overall race positions. Overall first receives 35 race points. Qualifying separately awards 3, 2, 1 points to the three fastest registered competitors/teams. The 35 is not an A-F driver/class-based award or necessarily the event total. Shortened-race treatment for H is not established by this passage.

translation.method: assistant factual translation verified against PDF extraction

passages.text: Written objections to race or championship points must reach the organizer within 14 days of publication. The organizer may correct obvious errors after publication. Complaints go to the organizer, and this clause states no appeal against its points decision. Read with Art. 3.2, this is not unlimited authority to change regulations.

provisions.summary: Championship points require received registration and fee; earlier results are excluded.

provisions.summary: A-F scoring uses final class rank and actual class starters, not overall race rank or registered field size.
provisions.applicability: NLS 2026 classifications A-F, including the annual overall championship, under this A1 version. Final class rank, actual starters and entitlement must be established for any event award.

Classification/sporting penalties may affect placing.

provisions.summary: Full-points class-winner awards depend on race format and seven actual class-starter bands.
provisions.applicability: Conditional A-F sole class winner, final class rank 1, eligible registered recipient and classified finish under this A1 version. For 1/2/3/4/5/6/7-or-more starters, 4h gives 2/3/4/6/8/11/15 and 6h gives 3/4/5/8/10/14/19 full points. No real event award is established.

These winner rows do not encode lower-rank awards or an exact race dead heat.
Seven starters is not a minimum scoring threshold.
No continuous formula or fractional-award rounding rule is inferred.
This class-based award is not automatically equivalent to Formula One overall-winner points.

profile.value: Conditional interpretation, pending translation review, of NLS 2026 A1 as at 12 June 2026 (after Bulletin 5). A-F championship scoring, including the annual overall championship, uses final CLASS rank and actual class starters, without deleting nonregistered starters. For an eligible registered sole class winner with 1/2/3/4/5/6/7-or-more actual starters, full-points 4h awards are 2/3/4/6/8/11/15; 6h awards are 3/4/5/8/10/14/19. Winner rows only; no continuous formula, lower-rank allocation or points-rounding rule is encoded. When distance is shortened or a stopped race is not resumed, 4h duration up to 80 minutes has no classification, over 80 through 160 half points, over 160 full; 6h up to 120 has no classification, over 120 through 250 half, over 250 full. Classification separately requires commercially rounded 70% class-winner AND 50% overall-winner distances, finish within 20 minutes and Art. 24 own-power/final-lap/pit-lane/finality conditions. Registration/fee, penalties, double-start nomination, season discards and points corrections remain material. Speed Trophy H's 35 overall-first race points are separate competitor/team context, not an A-F driver award, an equivalent Formula One comparison category or necessarily an event total. H reductions, exact race dead heats, full shared-car entitlement and incorporated DMSB stoppage details remain unresolved. B3 Art. 4 wording matches A1 but no unavailable prior Provision or fictional amends edge is created. Empty amends lists do not mean no amendments; B6-B8 concern technical changes in a bounded extraction scan, not a full amendment audit or proof of no indirect scoring effect. Only DMSB-approved German text is binding; the German 2025 versus English 2026 approval-date conflict is unresolved. Issue dates and effective periods are unknown. No event award or historical event applicability is established, and known does not mean reviewed, accepted or published.
